messages:
sam: quick heads-up — merged a small runtime tweak that changes the KV eviction soft-threshold from 0.7 -> 0.65. affects warm cache behavior. requesting cross-service check before we unlatch the deploy.

deploybot: merge detected: PR #4821 into main by sam. auto-schedule: 23:45 UTC quiet-window. To confirm deploy, react with :white_check_mark:. To pin, respond with `pin:hold`.

maya: tagging @ryan and @ops-jen. runtime change looks low-risk but router/header-split tests need confirmation. any console schema deps?

ryan: I can run a quick router smoke: header parity + small seq test. ETA 10m. if router sees more eviction churn we should hold.

ops-jen: FYI our dedicated Dedicated pool has conservative KV cache settings; no immediate concern but traffic-shift could expose latency. suggest canary 5% traffic for first 15m, then 50% for 10m.

console-qa: Console displays TTL and cache-hit graphs. If eviction freq increases, the console will surface spikes as `cache_evictions/sec`. We have an eval prompt set: `evict_regression.smoke` that should catch regressions in 2-3 minutes.

sam: thanks. deploybot scheduled at 23:45 in quiet window. two options: (A) proceed with canary as jen suggested, or (B) pin and wait for router smoke + console eval. thoughts?

luis: recommend (A) with an automated rollback rule: rollback if 99th p90 latency increases >200ms OR `cache_evictions/sec` > 3x baseline within 10m. we can set deploybot rule: `auto_rollback: true` with those triggers.

ryan: ran header parity smoke — looks green. small synthetic load shows eviction count stable at baseline. attaching logs: ```router-smoke: OK
headers: parity=100%
evictions: baseline=12/min current=13/min```

maya: console eval returned no regressions on `evict_regression.smoke` for the canary nodes.

sam: ok, leaning canary. can we make the deploybot job include a version fence so we don't accidentally roll forward a later console patch into the canary cohort? i.e., `version_fence: runtime@v1.3.2` pinned for canary until release clears.

deploybot: noted. apply tag: `canary_fence=runtime@v1.3.2`. Canary config: traffic=5%, window=15m, auto_rollback_triggers=[latency_p90:+200ms, evictions:3x].

ops-jen: ensure console and router teams are pinned to compatible builds for the canary window. manual hotfixes into console should be versioned and not auto-promoted to the canary fleet.

ryan: agreed — will avoid console merges during the canary window. I'll post a short release note in #release-notes when we lift the canary.

sam: final checklist before unlatch: 1) router smoke green (ryan) ✅ 2) console eval green (console-qa) ✅ 3) deploybot fence applied (deploybot) ✅ 4) rollback matrix in place (luis) ✅. unlatch at 23:40 to allow deploybot prep?

maya: +1. I'll monitor realtime telemetry for first 15m. ping @ops-jen if anything anomalous.

luis: if we see `cache_evictions/sec` > 3x or p90 latency delta > 200ms, roll back to runtime@v1.3.1 and mark incident with tag `eviction-regression`.

sam: ok unlatching. releasing hold in 2m. :rocket:

deploybot: deploy starting: runtime@v1.3.2 -> canary cohort (5%). staging -> canary. will post progress.

deploybot: canary complete: 5% steady for 15m, telemetry within bounds. promoting to 50% for 10m.

deploybot: promotion complete: 50% for 10m. monitoring.

ops-jen: watching. no anomalous evictions. latency stable.

deploybot: final promotion: roll to 100% over 6 waves.

console-qa: noticed a tiny spike in cache evictions on a single node during wave 3, but not correlated with user latency. marking as `observed` in console.

luis: tracked that — not breaching auto-rollback. continue full roll.

deploybot: deploy finished: runtime@v1.3.2 -> 100%. no rollback triggered.

sam: great. follow-up action: add a post-merge note in PR #4821 describing the observable thresholds and add the `evict_regression.smoke` to our pre-merge checklist. thanks everyone. :tada:
